{{Short description|Irish mathematician, astronomer and educator (1858–1928)}}
{{Use dmy dates|date=July 2026}}

'''Arthur Edward Lyster''' (28 June 1858 – 1928) was an Irish mathematician, astronomer and educator. He was elected a Foundation Scholar in Mathematics at [[Trinity College Dublin]] in 1883, served as an assistant at [[Dunsink Observatory]] from 1892 to 1896, and later taught mathematics at [[King's Hospital School, Dublin]]. He was the author of ''Mathematical Facts and Formulae'' (1899).<ref name="Atlas">{{cite web |title=The Atlas of Irish Mathematics: Kilkenny |url=https://www.mathsireland.ie/blog/2021_08_cm |access-date=19 July 2026 |website=Maths Ireland}}</ref>

The '''Arthur Lyster Prize''' in Mathematics at Trinity College Dublin was established in 1951 under the will of his sister, Mary Alice Lyster, and continues to be awarded by the university.<ref name="Prize">{{cite web |title=Prizes and Scholarships |url=https://www.maths.tcd.ie/prospective/prizesetc.php |access-date=19 July 2026 |website=School of Mathematics, Trinity College Dublin}}</ref>

== Early life ==
Lyster was born at Goresbridge, County Kilkenny, Ireland, on 28 June 1858.<ref name="Atlas" />

== Education ==
Lyster studied at [[Trinity College Dublin]], where he was elected a '''Foundation Scholar in Mathematics''' in 1883.<ref name="Atlas" /> He graduated Bachelor of Arts in 1885 and proceeded to the degree of Master of Arts in 1889.<ref name="Atlas" />

== Career ==
Between 1892 and 1896 Lyster served as an assistant at [[Dunsink Observatory]], then the observatory of Trinity College Dublin.<ref name="Atlas" />

Following his work at Dunsink he became Mathematics Master at King's Hospital School, Dublin.<ref name="Atlas" />

== Publications ==
Lyster was the author of:

* ''Mathematical Facts and Formulae'' (1899).<ref name="Atlas" />

The work was intended as a mathematical reference handbook for students and teachers.

== Legacy ==
Following the death of his sister Mary Alice Lyster, Trinity College Dublin received a bequest under her will in 1951 establishing the '''Arthur Lyster Prize''' in Mathematics. Trinity records that an additional sum was subsequently added by her executors.<ref name="Prize" />

The prize continues to be awarded to students in the School of Mathematics.<ref name="Prize" />

Lyster is buried with members of his family in the churchyard of All Saints Church, Newchurch, Isle of Wight.
